title: 5 Things about Miru: An Analog Adventure Game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TvvDTvo-L74

Daniel (@dungeondive) shares five things about Miru, Kelly Chance's zine-sized analog adventure game from Mimic Publishing Collective. First, the edition. The deluxe physical copy came with d20s, gems, a stapled journal and a bamboo pen, but he also prints his own play copy from the PDF. That sends him off on a tangent about his growing bookbinding hobby, with home-printed zines of Glide and an expansion for Alex T's Seekers Beyond the Threshold.

Second is the game itself. It's a hexcrawl with a bare-bones character: health, energy, attack, defence, combat manoeuvres to train, food, and "bitlets", a currency spun out of a failed billionaire's crypto token. Each day you pick a direction, roll the terrain, sketch it on the map and roll again for ruins, villages or encounters. Villages grow bigger as you find them, each with a shop, an inn and a quest. He reads out his journal: twisted ankles, starvation, a gas-station hot dog he still wouldn't eat, and a grolar bear beaten for a jewellery box.

Third, unlike most hexcrawls, Miru has a real story. A rogue robot kills your brother in 2125, and dated god events build towards a confrontation with the god of the robots. Fourth are the two DLC side-quest boards. Fifth is his wishlist: more side quests, random variants of the god events for replay value, and tighter wording on things like what impassable terrain does to your day. In his previous run, the same bear killed him on day two.

----

Daniel keeps a two-sentence journal for each day of a Miru run. Do you record your solo games, and does it change how you remember them?
